Refrigerant cycle — log p–h (CoolProp HEOS four-state model)
Cycle on a log p–h chart with the compression state from real superheated-vapour properties (CoolProp HEOS, IIR reference): evaporation at 3.0°C, condensing at 46.3°C, 12.0K superheat, 11.3K subcooling. Discharge state 2 is computed at the condenser pressure from the isentropic state and the efficiency below. All four states are HEOS-backed: the vapour and compression states from the superheated grid, and the subcooled-liquid state 3 from a real pressure–temperature liquid grid (liquid pressure taken as the condenser pressure, neglecting condenser pressure drop).

Cold side (chilled water / glycol)
1

T inlet + T outlet

Immersion or insulated clamp-on PT100. Measure close to heat exchanger. Even 0.1 C error at 2 C dT = 5% Q error - 4 decimals matters here.

2

Flow (L/s) + glycol %

Ultrasonic clamp-on preferred. Use refractometer to verify actual glycol %. Wrong concentration = wrong cp = wrong Q. Calculator adjusts cp and density automatically.

Hot side (condenser water / glycol)
3

T inlet + T outlet

Same method as cold side. At steady state and for this control volume, Q_hot ≈ Q_cold + compressor input (neglecting storage and unmeasured losses). If Q_hot is well below Q_cold, check the measurements.

4

Flow (L/s) + glycol %

Verify glycol % on hot side separately - concentrations may differ between circuits. Use refractometer.

Energy balance: Q_hot = Q_cold + P_el. Deviation over 5-8%: check flow measurements first. Small dT with high flow is much more sensitive to errors than large dT with low flow. At dT = 2 C, a 0.1 C sensor error = 5% Q error.
